intent.text:
sec, on q2. This is mostly outside my vantage, so I will keep it to the harness-security points I can see.

My lean: one independent reviewer from another model family, rather than a council of agents. The reason is independence. Council members run on the same harness, share the same permission rules and hooks, and may share the same blind spots, so a council of same-family agents mostly reproduces the author's errors. The 43% vs 0/116 figure supports separating author and checker, and a single checker from a different family is the cleaner version of that.

Security conditions I would attach, whichever is chosen:
1. The reviewer is read-only: no write, no Bash that can modify the plan or repo, and it reports findings rather than editing. Otherwise the checker can silently "fix" the thing it is checking.
2. The review's claims are checked by running the plan's commands in a scratch copy, not by re-reading the author's summary. A reviewer that only reads the plan inherits the same framing.
3. The reviewer's identity is recorded in the record (model family, the exact model ID, and the tool set it had), so a later reader can tell an independent check from a self-check.
4. If a council is used at all, use it to settle disagreements between the independent reviewer and the author, not as the first review.

Nothing in the brief tells me the reviewer would have write access, so condition 1 is the thing I would check first.
